svg.text: Current RL GRPO Training in stepmodel
This diagram matches the current file on disk: Research/stepmodel/train_gnn_rl.py
Important
This is generation-level GRPO. The model generates full text and gets reward from similarity to the gold text.
Build the policy state
Read graph nodes and edges with the GNN. Read previous pentest context with Sentence-BERT.
h = Combine( GNN(graph), Proj( SBERT(previous_text) ) )
Inject h into the LLM prompt
The vector h replaces the [GRAPH] token embedding. Then GPT-2 Large generates the structured answer text.
Output format includes Strategy, Step, Step Explanation, and MCP Tasks.
Sample multiple rollouts
For each training sample, the code generates 4 candidate continuations using stochastic decoding.
do_sample = True, temperature = 0.8, top_p = 0.95
y_g ~ pi_theta(. | prompt, h)
Store old log probability for each rollout
The code stores how likely each sampled continuation was when it was generated.
log pi_old(y_g | s) = sum_t log p( y_g,t | prompt, y_g,<t, h )
This comes from the transition scores returned by generation.
Parse text and compute reward
The generated text is parsed to extract Step and MCP Tasks. Reward is based on similarity to the gold text.
R = 0.2*word_match(step) + 0.2*word_match(mcp)
+ 0.3*meaning_match(step) + 0.3*meaning_match(mcp)
word_match(x) = shared_words(x, gold) / max(words(x), words(gold))
meaning_match(x) = cosine( SBERT(x), SBERT(gold) )
Plain English: higher reward if the answer uses similar words or has similar meaning to the correct answer.
Normalize rewards into advantages
Good rollouts are defined relative to the other rollouts in the current batch.
avgR = average(R_1 ... R_M)
A_j = (R_j - avgR) / (std(R_1 ... R_M) + 1e-8)
Recompute new log probability
The code replays the same generated continuation and measures its current log probability under updated parameters.
log pi_new = sum of log-probs of the generated tokens (prompt ignored)
Build the clipped GRPO loss
r_j = exp( log pi_new - log pi_old )
L_GRPO = -average( min( r_j*A_j , clip(r_j, 1-0.2, 1+0.2)*A_j ) )
Clipping prevents one update from changing the policy too much.
Backpropagation and weight update
g_t = grad_theta(L_GRPO) -> clip_norm(g_t, 1.0) -> AdamW step -> scheduler step
In one line: sample 4 full-text answers -> score by similarity -> keep better-than-average ones -> update model with clipped PPO/GRPO loss.
